title: Models and the Foundry catalog · Level 1
slo: Describe language models and use the Foundry catalog to find suitable models.

exercises.question_text: What can Microsoft Foundry help teams do? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: This is correct. Foundry includes a rich model catalog for discovery.
This is correct. Foundry supports both evaluation and flexible deployment.
This is correct. Operating models is part of Foundry's integrated environment.

options.text: Replace every model with a project.
options.error_type: Confuses a project workspace with a model
options.rationale: A project is a workspace for Foundry capabilities and client connections. It does not replace the models used in applications.
options.better_fit: Create a project to begin using Foundry capabilities.

feedback.intrinsic: The team would have a workspace but no model selected for its workload.
feedback.instructional: Projects organize Foundry work; models provide the generation and reasoning capabilities.

exercises.explanation: Correct! Foundry supports discovery, evaluation, deployment, and operation.

exercises.question_text: What is the basis of generative AI and agentic solutions?

options.rationale: This is correct. Language models provide the underlying intelligence for generative and agentic work.

options.error_type: Confuses models with a place to discover them
options.rationale: A catalog helps people discover and compare models. It does not generate responses.
options.better_fit: Use a model catalog when you need to find or compare models.

feedback.intrinsic: Choosing this would leave you with a place to browse, not a source of responses.
feedback.instructional: A catalog organizes model choices; language models generate the responses.

options.error_type: Confuses a workspace with model intelligence
options.rationale: A Foundry project is a workspace for capabilities and client connections. It is not the model that provides responses.
options.better_fit: Create a Foundry project when beginning work in Foundry.

feedback.intrinsic: You would set up a workspace but still need a model for responses.
feedback.instructional: A project provides the working space; a language model supplies the core intelligence.

options.error_type: Confuses a packaged component with its underlying model
options.rationale: An agent is built with a model, instructions, and optional actions. Its reasoning comes from the model it contains.
options.better_fit: Use an agent when reusable, task-oriented behavior is needed.

feedback.intrinsic: This names the packaged worker, not the intelligence it relies on.
feedback.instructional: Agents are built on top of models, so language models are the foundation.

exercises.explanation: Correct! Language models provide the underlying intelligence for generative and agentic work.

exercises.question_text: You can use Microsoft Foundry without an Azure subscription.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The setup would be missing a required starting condition.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use of Foundry requires an Azure subscription, then a Foundry project is created to begin.

exercises.explanation: Correct! An Azure subscription is required to use Foundry.

exercises.question_text: Language models are built on top of agents.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This reverses the relationship between the two.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Language models provide the basis, while agents package a model with instructions and optional actions.

exercises.explanation: Correct! The relationship goes in the other direction: agents are built with models.

exercises.question_text: Which statements describe a small language model (SLM)? Select all that apply.

options.text: It can fit a lightweight phone app.
options.rationale: This is correct. A lightweight phone application may run best on an SLM.

options.text: It is a type of language model.
options.rationale: This is correct. SLM means small language model.

options.text: It is always best for government apps.
options.error_type: Confuses lightweight needs with domain specialization
options.rationale: A government application may require a domain-specialized model. The source does not say an SLM is always best.
options.better_fit: Consider a domain-specialized model for a specialized government workload.

feedback.intrinsic: This could steer a specialized public-service workload toward the wrong kind of model.
feedback.instructional: Match the model to the workload. Lightweight phone apps and specialized government work can have different needs.

options.text: It is a catalog for finding models.
options.error_type: Confuses a model with the model catalog
options.rationale: An SLM is a model type. The model catalog is the hub for finding and comparing models.
options.better_fit: Use the model catalog when you need to discover models from providers.

feedback.intrinsic: This would confuse a response-generating model with the place used to find one.
feedback.instructional: An SLM is a language model; the catalog is for discovery and comparison.

exercises.explanation: Correct! An SLM is a language model that can suit a lightweight phone application.

exercises.question_text: Which filters can you use in the Foundry model catalog? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: This is correct. The catalog can filter models by source.
This is correct. Capabilities are one available catalog filter.
This is correct. The catalog can filter by inference tasks.

options.error_type: Confuses catalog filtering with an agent capability
options.rationale: Working memory is something agents can maintain during a conversation. It is not listed as a catalog filter.
options.better_fit: Consider working memory when describing what an agent can do in a conversation.

feedback.intrinsic: This would search for an agent behavior instead of narrowing model choices.
feedback.instructional: Catalog filters include source, capabilities, and inference tasks; working memory belongs to agents.

exercises.explanation: Correct! These filters help narrow a large set of model choices.

exercises.question_text: A small language model can be a good fit for a lightweight phone application.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This would overlook a model type that can fit a lightweight mobile need.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: SLMs can be a good fit for lightweight phone applications; model choice should match the workload.

exercises.explanation: Correct! A lightweight phone application may run best on an SLM.

exercises.question_text: Which models are hosted by Microsoft under Microsoft Product Terms?

options.rationale: This is correct. These models are hosted by Microsoft under Microsoft Product Terms.

options.error_type: Confuses vendor-hosted or open-source models with Azure-direct models
options.rationale: Partner and community models are open-source or vendor-hosted catalog models. That differs from Microsoft hosting under Microsoft Product Terms.
options.better_fit: Choose partner and community models for experimentation or specialized tasks.

feedback.intrinsic: This would assign the wrong hosting and sales description to the model source.
feedback.instructional: Microsoft-hosted models under Microsoft Product Terms are sold directly by Azure.

options.error_type: Confuses a broad model category with sales and hosting source
options.rationale: Foundation models are large pretrained models with general capabilities. That category does not specify Microsoft hosting terms.
options.better_fit: Use foundation model to describe a large pretrained base model.

feedback.intrinsic: The answer would identify a broad category rather than the hosting source.
feedback.instructional: The question asks about sales and hosting. Models sold directly by Azure have that description.

options.error_type: Confuses specialization with Azure hosting terms
options.rationale: Domain-tuned models are selected for industry-specific applications. Their specialization does not state who hosts them under which terms.
options.better_fit: Consider domain-tuned models for an industry-specific workload.

feedback.intrinsic: This would substitute task specialization for the required hosting detail.
feedback.instructional: Specialization and hosting source are different choices. Azure-direct models have the stated Microsoft hosting.

exercises.explanation: Correct! Models sold directly by Azure are hosted by Microsoft under Microsoft Product Terms.

exercises.question_text: The Foundry model catalog is a central hub for models from many providers.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This would overlook why the catalog is useful for comparing choices.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The catalog is a central hub for discovering and using models from an extensive range of providers.

exercises.explanation: Correct! The catalog brings together a wide selection of models from many providers.

exercises.question_text: What can a Foundry model entry include? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: This is correct. A model entry can include benchmark results and performance comparisons.
This is correct. Model entries can list supported fine-tuning options.
This is correct. Entries can include model cards, constraints, and caveats.

options.error_type: Confuses model entry details with an agent capability
options.rationale: An agent can break goals into structured steps and execute workflows. A model entry lists information about the model instead.
options.better_fit: Use an agent when a reusable component must carry out a workflow.

feedback.intrinsic: This would look for a completed worker process where model details should be reviewed.
feedback.instructional: Model entries provide capabilities, benchmarks, tasks, fine-tuning options, and responsible-use documentation.

exercises.explanation: Correct! These details help compare a model's fit, performance, and constraints.

exercises.question_text: Partner and community models are hosted by Microsoft under Microsoft Product Terms.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This switches the two model sources and their hosting descriptions.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Partner and community models are open-source or vendor-hosted catalog models; Azure-direct models are hosted by Microsoft.

exercises.explanation: Correct! That description belongs to models sold directly by Azure.

exercises.question_text: Fine-tuning means comparing models with benchmark results.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This would confuse customizing a model with measuring how models perform.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Fine-tuning adapts a pretrained model to a particular need. Benchmark results report performance comparisons.

exercises.explanation: Correct! Fine-tuning changes a pretrained model for a particular need; benchmarks compare performance.

flashcards.back: It is the basis of generative AI and agentic solutions.
It can fit a lightweight phone application.
It is the workspace for Foundry capabilities and client connections.
It adapts a pretrained model to a particular need.
